judgment_text:
The Judgment of the Court was delivered by

Sunder Mohan, J.:— The Criminal Appeal has been filed by sole accused, challenging the impugned order dated 08.12.2025, passed by the learned Special Judge (for exclusive trial of cases under SC/ST (POA) Act, 1989, Principal District and Sessions Court, Kancheepuram, in Crl.M.P. No. 2347 of 2025 in S.C. No. 92 of 2025, rejecting his bail application.

2. The appellant is accused of the offence under Sections 194(1) of BNSS @ 103(1) of BNS, Section 3(2)(v), 3(2)(va) of SC/ST (POA) Act.

3. The case of the prosecution is that the appellant and the victim had a love affair for more than ten years; that on the promise of marriage, the appellant had sexual intercourse with the victim; that since victim belonged to Scheduled Caste, the appellant did not get married to the victim; that since the victim pressurised the appellant to marry her, the appellant decided to cause the death of the victim; that on 02.04.2025 the appellant called the victim to a hotel, had sexual intercourse and while they were on the way to drop her to her house near a burial ground at about 11.30 p.m., the appellant had caused the death of the victim by attacking her with a hammer; and that thereafter, made it appear that the death was caused due to an accident by damaging the vehicle also and thus, committed the aforesaid offences.

4. The appellant sought for bail before the trial Court, which came to be dismissed by the impugned order dated 08.12.2025 on the ground that the appellant's bail application filed earlier was dismissed and the appeal filed before this Court also was dismissed on 01.11.2025, since there is no change in circumstances.

5. Mr. R. Vivekanandan, learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the case is based on circumstantial evidence; that the final report has now been filed; that the appellant's further incarceration is not required for the purpose of trial; that in the final report, it is stated that the occurrence took place between 11.30p.m., on 02.04.2025 and 12.30 a.m., on 03.04.2025; that it is contrary to the FIR which is registered on 02.04.2025 at about 8.30 a.m.; and that therefore considering the fact that the appellant is in custody from 03.04.2025, he prayed for bail.

6. Mr. S. Balaji, learned Government Advocate (Crl. Side) per contra submitted that this is the third appeal filed before this Court challenging the dismissal of his bail applications; and that this Court while dismissing the earlier appeal, had observed that the appellant had committed a very serious and heinous offence and there was no change in circumstances. He therefore opposed the grant of bail to the appellant as there was no change in circumstances.

7. Though the 3rd respondent/mother of the victim was served and none appeared on her behalf, this Court had appointed Mr. M. Ganesh, as legal aid counsel on 19.01.2026, to assist this Court on behalf of the 3rd respondent.

8. Mr. M. Ganesh, learned counsel for the 3rd respondent/defacto complainant would submit that the appellant had not only caused the death of the victim, but also attempted to screen the offence by making it appear that it was an accident; that it was a preplanned murder; that it was committed only because he did not want to marry the victim who belonged to Scheduled Caste community. Considering the gravity of the offence and since there is no change in circumstances, he prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

9. Admittedly this is the third appeal filed by the appellant challenging the dismissal of his bail application before this Court. His first appeal was dismissed on 19.06.2025 and the second appeal was dismissed on 27.11.2025 on the ground that the appellant had committed a grave offence and that there was no change in circumstances. The appellant is now in custody from 03.04.2025. The learned counsel for the defacto complainant also submitted that the appellant had not engaged any counsel and is attempting to protract the trial.

10. When the matter was listed on 04.02.2026, the learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the appellant had engaged a counsel and the case is now posted for charge framing on 17.02.2026.

11. The case is based on circumstantial evidence and it is for the prosecution to establish the circumstances before the trial Court. The appellant cannot be incarcerated pending trial for a long period and he has to defend himself effectively. However, this Court is of the view that it is desirable that the charges are framed before the appellant is released on bail. Therefore, this Court is not inclined to entertain this appeal at this stage and the same is dismissed with liberty to the appellant to approach the trial Court after the charges are framed, which may be considered by the trial Court on such conditions that the learned Judge deems fit to ensure that the appellant does not flee from justice.

12. With the above observations, the Criminal Appeal stands dismissed.
